articles.title: Zelenskyy can leverage Moscow ties from comedy days to make peace deal, says former key aide
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy earned his first millions in Moscow and should leverage those ties to negotiate with Vladimir Putin, says ex-aide.
articles.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's former spokesperson urged him Sunday to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin face-to-face in Moscow, arguing that his past business and political connections in the Russian capital from years back could help him negotiate a peace deal there. Iuliia Mendel, who served as Zelenskyy's spokesperson from 2019 to 2021, told Fox News Digital that the former comedian had also made his first millions in Russia and should perhaps leverage those ties to pursue lasting peace. "When Zelenskyy was an entertainer, he often performed in Moscow," Mendel said, adding that the Ukrainian president "knows a lot of people from Putin's elite." "He actually professionally grew in Moscow and earned his first millions in Moscow, and today he pretends that he has nothing in common with them," Mendel said. RECOVERING FROM LUNG SURGERY, POPE LEO URGES PUTIN TO AGREE TO CEASEFIRE IN RUSSIAN-HELD UKRAINE CITY "He needs to go to Moscow and needs to agree on compromises that are acceptable," she said, before adding that Zelenskyy "doesn't need to play his maximalist games and to play this noble actor." Mendel's criticism came as Ukraine, Russia and the United States prepared for another round of technical-level peace talks, potentially in Abu Dhabi or Switzerland, in November. U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have helped lay the groundwork for renewed negotiations that officials hope could finally lead to direct talks between the two leaders. Before entering politics, Zelenskyy had built a successful entertainment career. Beginning in the late 1990s, he performed with the comedy troupe Kvartal 95, competed on the Russian-language comedy program KVN and later worked as an actor, writer and producer in television and movies. From the late 1990s, he performed on Russian stages and at private parties and appeared in movies shown across former Soviet republics, Mendel claimed. She said that after Russia annexed Crimea and launched its war in Donbas in early 2014, Zelenskyy traveled to Russia to work on the comedy film "Eight New Dates" which was released in Russian theaters in 2015. ZELENSKYY TO SEEK OFFRAMP FOR YEARS-LONG RUSSIA WAR IN UN SPEECH AFTER TRUMP REVEALS PEACE DEAL IS CLOSE According to a report by Business Insider, many of Zelenskyy's movies were also in Russian and were marketed to a Russian audience, David Dodson, an American movie editor who worked with Zelenskyy told the outlet. "He was a well-loved comic, actor and performer in Russia, but after [the 2013-14] Maidan [Revolution], everything changed," Dodson said. "People need to realize that Volodya’s movies were very big in Russia. Most of his market was in Russia. He’s always been a popular comedy star in Russia," Dobson also clarified to GQ when asked if he directed the former actor in "Eight First Dates" in Russia, released in 2012. In 2013, the movie received the Russian National Movie Awards as the Best Russian Comedy of the Year. In 2019, Zelenskyy also promised to relinquish ownership of a Cyprus-registered company operating a film studio in Russia after investigative journalists revealed that he and his business partners still owned three Russian companies, according to the Kyiv Post. Zelenskyy's entertainment career made him a household name in Ukraine and other former Soviet republics before he entered politics and won Ukraine's 2019 presidential election with roughly 73% of the runoff vote on promises to fight corruption and pursue peace in eastern Ukraine. Mendel argued that Zelenskyy's promise to bring peace at the time stands in stark contrast to the devastating war that has crippled the country and defined much of his presidency. TRUMP ANNOUNCES IMMEDIATE ENERGY CEASEFIRE BETWEEN RUSSIA AND UKRAINE "Zelenskyy became the president with 73% record support," Mendel said. "Because he promised to bring peace to Ukraine." "And now he has been presiding for almost five years (over) the largest war in Europe since World War II. This shows a lot." "When his country is bleeding, he needs to make a peace deal for his people," she said before adding that the leader "needs to put the interests of his people first, just for Ukraine to exist as an independent state." Whether Zelenskyy should travel to Moscow has, in fact, become a flashpoint in efforts to arrange direct peace talks. In 2025, Putin offered to host Zelenskyy for talks in Moscow, but the Ukrainian president rejected the invitation as Russian forces continued attacking Ukraine. "He can come to Kyiv," Zelenskyy told ABC News at the time, saying he could not visit Moscow while Ukraine remained under Russian missile attacks. In September, on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly, Russian journalists pressed Zelenskyy on when he would visit Moscow. He replied, "On a missile." ZELENSKYY CONGRATULATES TRUMP ON TURNING 80 IN BIRTHDAY CALL, VOWS MORE UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AT G7 ON TUESDAY Mendel, however, argued that personal animosity between the two leaders has become the main obstacle to diplomacy. "Today there are diplomatic efforts to try to stop this brutal and bloody war that Russia started," she said. "But what we see now is a personal opposition between Zelenskyy and Putin that continues to grow into constant escalation in which people suffer tremendously, Ukraine's infrastructure, energy grid, and businesses are in ruins, and refugees are fleeing." Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. More than four years later, peace negotiations are deadlocked over territory, security guarantees and the terms of a lasting ceasefire. Moscow has demanded territorial concessions from Ukraine, including areas Russian forces do not fully control. Kyiv has rejected ceding sovereign territory and insists that any agreement include enforceable security guarantees against another Russian attack. RUSSIA RELEASES AMERICAN TEACHER IMPRISONED ON UKRAINE MERCENARY CHARGES AFTER TRUMP PRESSED PUTIN Mendel went on to praise President Donald Trump's efforts to break the diplomatic deadlock, calling him the first Western leader to "challenge the status quo" and consistently push for an end to the war. "For this reason, many Ukrainians place great hope in his ability to bring peace," she said. "A sustainable peace deal cannot be reached solely between Zelensky and Putin; it requires the involvement and initiative of a strong third party to halt the ongoing devastation." On Friday, the White House announced that first lady Melania Trump had helped broker a temporary ceasefire in Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in southern Ukraine's Kherson region, to allow humanitarian aid deliveries, demining operations and civilian evacuations. An estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people remain in the devastated front-line town, many of them facing severe shortages of food, medicine and other essentials. The White House said the ceasefire would begin Oct. 29, although Ukrainian and Russian officials have indicated that operations could begin Oct. 27. Pope Leo also reportedly spoke with Zelenskyy and Putin about the humanitarian crisis, according to Vatican News. ZELENSKYY ACCUSES PUTIN OF DEFYING TRUMP'S CEASEFIRE PUSH, SENDS POINTED MESSAGE TO WHITE HOUSE "Melania Trump has become synonymous with the words of a saver and a hero, since she has brokered the deal for Oleshky," Mendel said. "This is something that is going to save around 2,000 people and that neither Ukraine nor Russia could have solved for months and months." "That is why, you know, what Melania Trump has done is actually a case to show that where two men are fighting, a woman can actually save lives," she added. "And this is the new approach that would show that peace really should focus on human lives, not on maps and territories." Mendel also criticized the influence of Zelenskyy's longtime ally Andriy Yermak on his diplomatic approach, arguing that the Ukrainian president has favored confrontation over compromise. "Mr. Yermak was teaching Zelenskiy to be a strong man in diplomacy. And what today we see is actually diplomacy that doesn't exist," she said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "It's a diplomacy of humiliation, diplomacy of constant threats, diplomacy of demands," Mendel added.

articles.title: Raids on NE drug cartels reveal illicit deals worth Rs 270cr
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In a major crackdown on cross-border narco-hawala networks in northeastern states, multi-agency search operations by at least 38 teams at 38
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a major crackdown on cross-border narco-hawala networks in northeastern states, multi-agency search operations by at least 38 teams at 38 locations simultaneously, revealed illicit transactions of over Rs 270 crore, and led to arrest of six people and freezing of over 1,425 mule bank accounts. Properties worth over Rs 26 crore were also frozen or attached during the searches.“Modi govt’s lethal blow against drugs continues... Our agencies launched a barrage of simultaneous crackdowns across 38 locations in Assam, Mizoram and Manipur on Oct 23, smashing an international narco-cartel,” Union home minister Amit Shah said Sunday. Shah said India will hammer until the last nail is driven into the coffin of drug cartels.He also outlined govt’s policy of ‘zero tolerance’ against drugs and the strategic shift from a seizure-centric to a network-centric approach. The drive is part of Centre’s mission to eradicate drug smuggling syndicates by 2029.The latest searches were conducted on several premises in Aizawl, Champhai and Lawngtlai and Churachandpur and were related to cross-border trafficking of heroin, brown sugar and methamphetamine tablets from Myanmar and hawala settlement of drug proceeds. The operation was conducted by ED in coordination with NCB and Mizoram Police.ED has identified layered transactions of over Rs 270 crore, handled by illicit money exchangers, or hawala network, in Champhai, including Rs 125 crore in cash received from Assam, Nagaland, Bengal, Tripura and Delhi.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Panchang Today, October 26, 2026: Shukla Paksh 15 (Purnima), Ashwini, Shubh Muhurat, Rahu Kaal and More
articles.summary: Panchang Today is your everyday compass, built on the Hindu calendar’s deep sense of time and rhythm.
articles.body: Panchang Today is your everyday compass, built on the Hindu calendar’s deep sense of time and rhythm. It tells you what the Moon is doing, which star is active, and which parts of the day support work, worship, travel, and family choices. In a busy life, this small pause for Panchang keeps you connected to your cultural roots, and it also helps you act with more care, not just speed. Think of it like checking the sky before you step out, you plan better. Below are the important Panchang details for October 26, 2026 for India:Date & Day DetailsDate & Day DetailsOctober 26, 2026 falls on a Monday, a day that naturally leans toward steadiness, responsibilities, and the mind’s quieter routines. The Tithi is Shukla Paksh 15 (Purnima), and it ends at 09:41:18, after which the next Tithi begins, Krishan Paksh 1 (Pratipada(Ekam)). Purnima is the full Moon, the peak of the waxing fortnight. Spiritually, it’s like the Moon holds a mirror up to your emotions. Things become clear. Feelings rise, memories surface, and intentions made earlier in the month demand a practical step now.Because the Purnima Tithi completes at 09:41:18, the morning carries that full, luminous energy. This is supportive for prayer, gratitude, completing pending tasks, and family discussions that need warmth and honesty. After the shift to Pratipada(Ekam), the day’s tone subtly changes. Pratipada is the first step of the waning cycle, a clean page. It’s good for beginning simple habits, setting a fresh routine, and deciding what to reduce, clutter, overspending, gossip, unhealthy food, the usual suspects.The Nakshatra is Ashwini, ending at 17:41:15, after which Bharani takes over. Ashwini is ruled by the Ashwini Kumars, the divine healers and swift riders of the sky. That makes the day feel quick. You may want to rush, reply fast, finish fast, move fast. Use it well. Ashwini supports healing actions, starting exercise, visiting for checkups, learning a new skill, and timely travel. It also favours solutions that are simple and immediate, not overthought.By evening, Bharani begins. Bharani is linked with Yama, the keeper of dharma and discipline. So the day moves from speed to seriousness, like the breeze becoming firmer after sunset. If you’ve been avoiding a duty, Bharani’s influence can bring it right in front of you. Good. Handle it.The Moon sign is Aries 6.20, and it stays in Aries through the day, with a transition to Taurus at 27/10/2026 21:06:41. Aries Moon makes emotions direct. People speak plainly. Patience can run thin, especially in queues, traffic, and family group chats. Yet it’s excellent for taking initiative and not waiting for someone else to do the job.The Yoga is Vajra, ending at 14:16:55, and then Siddhi begins. Vajra has a tough, thunderbolt-like quality. It can make you determined, sometimes stubborn. Use it for disciplined work, not arguments. Siddhi later brings smoother outcomes, the kind where effort starts showing results. Karan also shapes the day’s flavour. Bava Karan lasts until 09:41:18, then Balava continues until 20:24:06. These are steady, workable Karans, helpful for routine progress, paperwork, household organisation, and commitments you can actually keep.Auspicious Timings (Shubh Muhurat)Auspicious Timings (Shubh Muhurat)Some days feel like the door opens easily if you knock at the right moment. Today has several such windows, and they’re worth using for prayer, decisions, and important steps.Brahma Muhurta runs from 2026-10-26 04:20:38 to 2026-10-26 05:11:22. This is the quiet, pre-dawn pocket when the mind is clean and receptive. If you’ve been trying to restart meditation, study, or a spiritual vow, this is the best time to sit with it. Even 15 minutes of japa or silent breathing here can change your mood for the whole day.Pratah Sandhya is from 2026-10-26 04:46:00 to 2026-10-26 06:02:06. It’s ideal for Surya arghya, simple prayers, and setting an intention for the day. On Purnima, morning worship feels fuller, like the heart has more space.Amrit Kalam appears from 2026-10-26 10:59:35 to 2026-10-26 12:28:47. This is a sweet stretch for important calls, submitting forms, starting a key meeting, or doing Satyanarayan Puja with focus. If you need to ask for help or approval, do it in this window. People respond better.Abhijit Muhurta, from 2026-10-26 11:18:58 to 2026-10-26 12:04:14, is another strong slot for beginning something that needs success and clarity. It’s particularly useful for interviews, signing something small but meaningful, or making a firm commitment to a health routine.Vijay Muhurta runs from 2026-10-26 13:34:46 to 2026-10-26 14:20:02. It supports winning energy. Use it to push a stuck task forward, speak to your boss about a pending matter, or tackle that one piece of work you keep postponing.In the evening, Godhuli Muhurta is from 2026-10-26 17:21:33 to 2026-10-26 17:46:55, and Sayahana Sandhya lasts from 2026-10-26 17:21:33 to 2026-10-26 18:37:39. These are perfect for lighting a diya, doing aarti, and calming the house atmosphere. On Sharad Purnima, twilight worship feels especially comforting.Night holds Nishita Muhurta from 2026-10-26 23:16:41 to 2026-10-27 00:07:25, a powerful time for deep prayer, mantra, and quiet inner work.Choghadiya also gives practical help. Day auspicious periods include Amrit @ 06:01, Shubh @ 08:51, Laabh @ 14:31, and Amrit @ 15:56. Night auspicious periods include Laabh @ 22:06, Shubh @ 25:17, and Amrit @ 26:52. Pick these for errands that matter, payments you must make, or family discussions that need a softer tone.Inauspicious TimingsInauspicious TimingsEvery day has a few rough patches, like a sudden patch of stones on an otherwise smooth road. The Panchang doesn’t ask you to fear them, it asks you to be smart.Rahu Kaal today is 07:26 to 08:51. There is also a verified Rahu Kaal window listed as 2026-10-26 07:27:01 to 2026-10-26 08:51:57. In essence, this morning period is best kept free from new beginnings. Don’t start a new business pitch, don’t sign a contract, and don’t make a big financial decision here. Keep your wallet closed today during this slot. If you must work, do routine work only.What should you do in Rahu Kaal? Choose inner work over outer risk. Sit for a short meditation, chant the Rahu mantra “Om Raam Rahave Namaha”, or simply read a few lines of a spiritual text. If you’re commuting, keep your mind quiet and avoid needless arguments.Yamaganda is from 2026-10-26 10:16:53 to 2026-10-26 11:41:49. This time can bring impatience and small obstacles. Avoid launching something new. Delay a hard confrontation if you can. If a meeting can be moved, move it.Gulika Kaal, shown as gulkai_kaal, runs from 2026-10-26 13:06:45 to 2026-10-26 14:31:41. This period is best for routine tasks and follow-ups, not for taking a big leap. Keep discussions practical. Avoid impulsive purchases.Dur Muhurtam appears twice, from 2026-10-26 12:04:14 to 2026-10-26 12:49:14, and again from 2026-10-26 14:20:02 to 2026-10-26 15:05:02. These are not ideal for initiating important work, sending risky emails, or making promises you can’t keep. Use these blocks for admin work, cleaning up your inbox, or finishing small tasks.Varjyam is from 2026-10-27 02:30:39 to 2026-10-27 03:58:33. It’s a time to avoid important starts and avoid restless late-night decision making. Sleep is a better choice.There’s also Baana (Roga) from 2026-10-26 06:02:06 to 2026-10-26 21:04:06. Treat this as a reminder to respect the body. Don’t skip meals and then overeat later. Don’t ignore small signs of fatigue.Panchaka runs from 2026-10-26 06:02:06 to 2026-10-27 06:02:40. Traditionally, Panchaka asks for extra care in planning and execution. It doesn’t mean you stop life. It means you double-check. Lock doors properly, confirm tickets, re-read messages before sending.Aadal Yoga is from 2026-10-26 17:41:59 to 2026-10-27 06:02:40, beginning just after Ashwini ends and the evening mood shifts. It can stir restlessness or sudden changes in plans. Don’t pick fights at home at night. Keep dinner light and conversations kinder.Choghadiya inauspicious periods also matter. Day inauspicious slots include Kaal @ 07:26, Rog @ 10:16, and Udveg @ 11:41. Night inauspicious slots include Rog @ 18:56, Kaal @ 20:31, and Udveg @ 23:42. During these, do regular work, not high-stakes work.Rahu Kaal Timings Across IndiaRahu Kaal Timings Across IndiaRahu Kaal changes across India because it is calculated from local sunrise, and sunrise differs from place to place due to longitude. So even on the same date, one region’s Rahu Kaal won’t exactly match another’s. The table below shows Rahu Kaal for major Indian cities, so you can follow the timing closest to your location and plan your important starts accordingly.CityRahu KaalMumbai08:02 - 09:29Delhi (NCR)07:52 - 09:16Bengaluru07:39 - 09:07Hyderabad07:39 - 09:05Chennai07:28 - 08:56Ahmedabad08:06 - 09:32Pune07:58 - 09:24Kolkata07:03 - 08:28Jaipur07:56 - 09:21Kochi07:42 - 09:11Lucknow07:36 - 09:00Indore07:53 - 09:19Guwahati06:52 - 08:17Chandigarh07:55 - 09:19Surat08:04 - 09:30Visakhapatnam07:20 - 08:46Nagpur07:39 - 09:05Coimbatore07:40 - 09:09Varanasi07:26 - 08:51Bhubaneswar07:11 - 08:37Sunrise, Sunset, Moonrise & MoonsetSunrise, Sunset, Moonrise & MoonsetSunrise is at 06:01:57, and that first light has its own message on Purnima. Wake up with purpose. Even a simple act, washing the face, offering water, standing quietly near a window, becomes a small reset. The day’s sunlight runs until sunset at 17:21:32. Use the middle hours wisely, because Aries Moon can make you burn energy fast. Pace yourself. Eat on time. Keep water nearby.Moonrise happens at 05:12:44 PM, and moonset is at 07:08:22 AM, Oct 27. articles.summary: A Beverly Hills home once owned by Hollywood actor Tom Cruise has changed hands for about $47 million, nearly a decade after the star sold it to
articles.body: A Beverly Hills home once owned by Hollywood actor Tom Cruise has changed hands for about $47 million, nearly a decade after the star sold it to billionaire Leon Black for $38 million in 2016. The property, which dates back to the 1930s, sits on approximately 1.2 acres and includes a main residence spanning around 10,000 square feet. Its latest sale marks another chapter in the history of the estate, which has remained largely out of public view.Tom Cruise’s former Beverly Hills home sold for $47 millionAccording to The Wall Street Journal, Black, the former chief executive of Apollo Global Management, sold the property for approximately $47 million. The buyer’s identity was not immediately known, and the house was not publicly advertised when the deal took place.The sale was handled privately, with local estate agents telling that the property had been quietly offered to potential buyers away from the open market. Linda May of Carolwood Estates and Fred Bernstein of Westside Estate Agency represented Black in the transaction, while the buyer was represented by real estate agent Kurt Rappaport.The latest transaction comes after a decade of ownership by Black and his wife, Debra Black, who purchased the estate through a limited liability company in 2016.What made the property notable during Cruise’s ownershipAs reported by the Los Angeles Times in June 2016, Cruise sold the Beverly Hills estate for $38 million after purchasing it in 2007 for $30.5 million. The actor had acquired the property from real estate developer and agent Kurt Rappaport, completing the purchase through a private transaction.The estate had been quietly offered for sale the previous year, with an asking price of $50 million. Its eventual sale price was therefore below that initial figure.Cruise's decision to sell the property was part of a broader effort to reduce his real estate holdings. The actor had also sold a gated compound in Hollywood Hills West for $11.4 million in 2015. His large retreat in Telluride, Colorado, had also been put on the market around that time. The Beverly Hills property was among the more significant assets associated with the actor's residential portfolio.Inside the 1930s estate and its groundsThe Los Angeles Times reported a gated and landscaped estate centred on a main house measuring more than 10,000 square feet. The residence contained 7 bedrooms, 9 full bathrooms and 35 rooms in total.The grounds offered several amenities, including a swimming pool, a tennis and basketball court, lawns and formal landscaping. Two detached structures also formed part of the estate, while a large motor court provided space for vehicles near the entrance.Why did Leon Black decide to sell the houseBlack and his wife sold the property because they no longer needed it, according to the WSJ. Their two adult children had lived and worked in Los Angeles for a period, but both subsequently returned to New York. As a result, the family had little reason to continue maintaining a large residence in Beverly Hills.Black, who co-founded Apollo Global Management in 1990, stepped down as the firm's chief executive in 2021.The sale comes during a challenging period for Los Angeles propertyThe $47 million transaction stands out against a slower period for the Los Angeles residential property market. Local agents had attributed the slowdown over the preceding year partly to the devastating Los Angeles wildfires and the departure of wealthy residents for states with lower taxes.Against this backdrop, the sale of Black's Beverly Hills estate ranks among the area's larger property transactions in recent months. The estate has passed through two prominent owners over nearly two decades.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Data centre debate heats up ahead of US midterms - here's what you need to know
articles.summary: Data centres are the lifeblood of our digital world, but there are growing concerns about their environmental impact. The BBC explores their rise in charts.
articles.body:
Until a few years ago many of us may have been blissfully unaware of what a data centre was.

These giant, warehouse-like buildings power virtually all our internet activity, from our web searches and emails to movie downloads and online banking.

They are at the heart of the AI boom, housing the advanced computer chips and servers needed to run services like ChatGPT and Claude.

But the speed at which they're growing, the enormous amount of electricity they consume and concerns about their environmental impact are fuelling a public backlash around the world.

In the US, they've become a huge issue ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November, with both Republicans and opposition Democrats coming out against their development.

It's putting opponents of data centre expansion on a collision course with US President Donald Trump, who has dismissed the pushback as a "sick conspiracy", even as public anger grows.

Here's what you need to know about the data centre boom, and why opposition is growing.

There are about 12,250 data centres around the world, according to Data Center Map , a company that tracks both operational and pre-operational sites.

That's up sharply from 2021, when there were around 8,000 operational sites.

As the chart below shows, data centres are most densely clustered in the US which has 4,767 sites. It is followed by Europe, where the UK and Germany lead.

Data centres have typically been located near to cities where it's easier to access high voltage power lines or water resources for cooling. But as they get bigger, more are being built in rural areas.

But when it comes to actual capacity, the US is ahead by a much larger margin, with China in second place and Europe lagging far behind.

This gap is set to widen in the coming years, leading some to warn Europe risks missing out on the potential economic benefits of the AI boom .

Data centres vary wildly in size, ranging from ones that fit inside a garden shed to others covering vast expanses of land.

The world's largest operational data centre is widely reported to be one run by China Telecom in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia, covering an area of approximately one million square metres (10.7 million sq ft). That is equivalent to about 140 Fifa football pitches.

However, much larger sites are under construction as the graphic below shows.

All these sites are being built exclusively to provide the immense computing power needed to run AI services.

For instance, Colossus 2, which is part of the wider Colossus campus, will house hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips made by tech giant Nvidia.

It will also be used to train xAI's chatbot Grok. Elon Musk's company will use 41 methane gas turbines to help power the site, which activists say could "significantly increase" local air pollution . Local regulators say the turbines will meet air quality standards.

The pressure data centres put on local resources has sparked increasing concern. These facilities can use significant amounts of water to cool their systems, which could lead to water shortages , some experts say.

Data centres worldwide are also thought to consume more electricity than the whole of France, as the chart below shows.

This growing hunger for power is driving up carbon emissions, analysis shows , while putting pressure on local grids, which some fear could push up energy prices .

With others worried about the noise data centres make and the space they take up, a public backlash is gathering steam.

Some 16 US states have proposed laws to ban or temporarily block new facilities, and it could be a key issue in November's midterm elections .

Outside the US, opposition to data centres has emerged in countries like Mexico , France, Indonesia and the UK .

But supporters say data centres are critical to national security , and the development of AI.

They also say they are good for the economy , attracting investment, generating tax revenue and creating jobs in areas like construction.

A recent report by the Brookings Center suggests data centres do create local jobs, although fewer than industry advocates claim.

The type of data centre matters too. So-called hyperscale facilities - massive sites owned and run by tech giants like Amazon and Microsoft - have a bigger positive effect on jobs, it found.

But "colocation" facilities, which lease space to remote tenants without a local presence, brought fewer benefits.

As the debate over their merits intensifies, the data centre rollout continues.

This year, the tech industry is expected to spend a combined $765bn ($544bn) on AI infrastructure in 2026, with this topping $1tn next year.

But as concerns about the environmental impact grow, the tech industry is exploring alternatives.

One idea is to put data centres in space or on the Moon , where they could harness abundant solar energy.

Others predict that more AI processing could eventually be carried out by the hardware already inside our computers and smartphones , reducing the need for vast data centres altogether.

articles.title: From India’s Gir forest to Edinburgh: New hope for big cats, as zoo welcomes two endangered Asiatic lion cubs for the first time in seven years
articles.summary: Imagine waiting for nearly a decade for something, and finally landing two of them!
articles.body: Imagine waiting for nearly a decade for something, and finally landing two of them!After seven years of waiting, Edinburgh Zoo finally has something exciting to celebrate: two brand new Asiatic lion cubs. These little arrivals aren’t just adorable; they have a much bigger meaning. Their birth on October 11, 2026, marks not only a rare event for the zoo but also highlights how vital conservation efforts are for one of the planet’s most endangered big cats. Their mother, Bindee, is a first-time parent, and their father, Jayendra, or Jay, as the keepers call him, seems to be taking everything in stride.What happened?Word got out about the cubs on October 22, when the Royal Zoological Society of Scotland (RZSS), which runs Edinburgh Zoo, made the big announcement. Keepers had a front-row seat thanks to cameras in the lions’ den; they watched the births unfold and have been keeping a close eye on Bindee and her cubs ever since. At the moment, the zoo is keeping the family out of sight of visitors so that Bindee can bond with her new babies in peace. They've closed the lion habitat for now and promised to keep everyone updated about when things might reopen.It’s especially meaningful because the last time lion cubs were born at Edinburgh Zoo was in 2019, so there’s been quite a wait. The fresh arrivals aren’t just a win for the zoo; they’re a way to shine a spotlight on the real challenges facing Asiatic lions. In the wild, these cats hang on in just one small patch of India.As reported by the Edinburgh News, RZSS’s animal team leader, Alison MacLean, sounded genuinely delighted when talking about Bindee’s excellent care of her cubs. As for Jay, he’s apparently as laid-back as ever. But right now, the zoo’s staff care most about the health of the cubs, and the first few months are crucial. The family will stay mostly tucked away, with Bindee doing the heavy lifting as a new mom, and keepers watching quietly from behind the scenes.Meet Bindee and Jay: The lion parents with a storyWho are the proud parents, you ask? Bindee, ten years old, came to Edinburgh Zoo in 2024 from France, while Jay, fifteen, arrived in 2012 from Bristol Zoo, having been born in 2010. The keepers started guessing Bindee might be pregnant when they noticed her belly grow and her movements slow down. She became even more suspicious when she started changing up her den, pacing and prepping for her new arrivals.This birth is big news, especially since it’s Bindee’s first litter. Thanks to those cameras, zookeepers got to watch the birth unfold without interrupting Bindee’s natural instincts. The zoo says she’s doing well and bonding nicely with her cubs, much like any wild lioness would.Right now, the cubs are just getting used to life inside their den, and they’re not quite ready to meet the world. It’ll likely be several months before visitors get their first glimpse. As for their names? No update on that yet. The zoo is keeping everything under wraps, putting the little lions’ well-being above all else. The lion habitat stays closed while the animal-care team waits for just the right moment.Why the birth matters: The plight of Asiatic lionsNow, about the significance of these cubs, it goes way beyond Edinburgh. Asiatic lions, known scientifically as Panthera leo persica, have been nearly wiped out by hunting and the destruction of their habitat. In the past, they roamed across western and southern Asia. Today, their last wild survivors stick to a single region: the Gir forest and its surrounding areas in Gujarat, India.That’s exactly why there’s a glimmer of hope in this story.As shared by PIB (Press Information Bureau), in India’s 2025 count, officials recorded 891 lions, up from 674 just five years prior. That’s a 32% jump, and the numbers include cubs, subadults, and adults scattered across the lion landscape, even outside the main protected area. But a bigger population doesn’t mean the species is safe. When a species lives in just one area, it’s super vulnerable. Disease, disasters, and even accidents can threaten the whole group at once. Meanwhile, lions that wander outside the protected zone face dangers from roads, trains, and clashes with people and livestock.So, they’re still in trouble. The International Union for Conservation of Nature lists the Asiatic lion as endangered. Protecting their habitat, providing veterinary care, monitoring populations, and finding ways to reduce human-lion conflict — all of this is essential if these lions have a chance at a future.How Edinburgh Zoo fits into the bigger pictureEdinburgh Zoo doesn’t just display lions; it plays a real part in conservation. The RZSS runs the place and takes part in the European Endangered Species Programme for Asiatic lions. The programme tries to keep the population healthy and genetically diverse inside zoos, while boosting awareness, funding research, and supporting lions in the wild. So, these two new cubs are a lot more than just cute faces; they matter to the survival of the entire species, whether in zoos or back home in India.The birth also gives Edinburgh Zoo a chance to teach visitors about wildlife conservation, showing how the lives of animals in captivity really connect to the challenges their wild cousins face. Sure, breeding in zoos can’t replace wild populations, but it helps keep genetic diversity, fosters research, and grabs people’s attention, which is half the battle when it comes to saving endangered creatures.For now, Bindee and her cubs are hunkered down out of sight, slowly growing and getting stronger before their big debut. After so many years without lion cubs, the zoo’s staff are thrilled. It’s a feel-good moment, and a reminder that every new cub matters when a species is fighting for survival.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Todd Blanche challenges Dana Bash for only citing part of Constitution during heated election clash
articles.summary: Todd Blanche demanded CNN show the full Elections Clause in the Constitution on air after Dana Bash highlighted only the first portion during a tense legal debate.
articles.body: Attorney General Todd Blanche confronted CNN host Dana Bash on Sunday after the network highlighted only the first portion of the Constitution's Elections Clause during a heated exchange on "State of the Union" over the Justice Department's lawsuit concerning two candidates with similar names in Alaska's closely watched Senate race. Blanche pushed back as Bash referenced the Alaska Supreme Court's earlier ruling allowing Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., who shares a name with incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, to remain on the ballot. The attorney general demanded that CNN display the remainder of the constitutional provision, which grants Congress authority to make or alter regulations governing congressional elections. "Conveniently, you put up the Constitution on your screen, but you highlighted only the first clause. Why don't you show the next clause to your viewers, which says that Congress is allowed to pass laws to make sure that that happens? Put that back up there," Blanche said. BLANCHE WON'T RULE OUT DOJ BLOCKING ELECTION CERTIFICATION IN 'DOOMSDAY' SCENARIO The exchange centered on Article I, Section 4 of the Constitution, which gives state legislatures authority to establish procedures for congressional elections while permitting Congress to enact or modify those regulations. Blanche argued that the second half of the provision supports the federal government's intervention under existing federal statutes. "The second clause says that the Congress may at any time by law, and we have a law, and that's the law that we're relying on when we filed suit earlier this week," Blanche said. The Justice Department’s lawsuit relies on the National Voter Registration Act, arguing that allowing a candidate who, according to the DOJ, intends to confuse voters to remain on the ballot undermines election integrity. The complaint asks the court to delay election certification if votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. could alter the final outcome. The DOJ's complaint accused the challenger of deliberately attempting to mislead voters by using a name similar to the incumbent's. DOJ OFFICIAL DEFENDS TRUMP'S NONCITIZEN VOTER PROBE ON '60 MINUTES,' ACCUSES SHOW OF EDITING OUT HER ANSWERS Media Research Center President David Bozell criticized Bash's presentation of the constitutional language in a statement to Fox News Digital, accusing CNN of failing to provide viewers with the complete provision. "An anchor who hands viewers half a provision on election integrity is running a magic act, and the trick fell apart on live television. Bash's job is to give the audience the full text up front. CNN owes its dozens of viewers the whole clause, and a better editor," Bozell said. The DOJ lawsuit follows a June ruling by the Alaska Supreme Court allowing the challenger to appear on the ballot despite objections from state election officials. The court left the question of how his name should appear to the state's Division of Elections. "Daniel J. Sullivan decided to run for Senator in 2026 as a Republican with the intention of misleading supporters of Senator Sullivan into voting for him," the complaint states. BLANCHE ANNOUNCES CHARGES AGAINST 10 PERMANENT RESIDENTS ACCUSED OF MINNESOTA VOTER FRAUD Republicans have accused the challenger, a retired teacher from Petersburg, of attempting to siphon votes from the incumbent. Daniel J. Sullivan has denied those accusations and maintained that his candidacy is legitimate.
